title: NIELIT Hyderabad and QClairvoyance Train Over 200 Students in Quantum Technology
html:
Insider Brief

  • NIELIT Hyderabad and QClairvoyance Quantum Labs conducted a three-day quantum technology workshop for more than 200 students from nine educational institutions.
  • The November 11-13 programme covered quantum communication, quantum algorithms, quantum key distribution, quantum teleportation and post-quantum cryptography, alongside practical exercises and laboratory demonstrations.
  • In a post-workshop survey, 70 of 73 respondents said they would or might consider a career in quantum technology or quantum security, while the average feedback rating was 4.6 out of 5.
  • Image from Pexels by Amit Rai.

PRESS RELEASE — More than 200 students from nine educational institutions participated in a three-day workshop on emerging trends in quantum communications and applications in quantum technology, organised by NIELIT Hyderabad under the Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY). Held at the NIELIT Hyderabad campus from November 11 to 13, the programme was conducted by experts from QClairvoyance Quantum Labs Pvt. Ltd.

The workshop brought together students from Scient Institute of Technology, Ibrahimpatnam; Aurora’s PG College, Panjagutta; AVN Institute of Engineering and Technology; CMR Technical Campus; Sarojini Naidu Vanita Maha Vidyalaya; RVR & JC College of Engineering; Muffakham Jah College of Engineering and Technology; Sun International Institute of Tourism and Management; and Government Degree College for Women, Begumpet.

Students from Computer Science, AI/ML, Data Science, Electronics and Communication, Electrical Engineering, Management and Commerce programmes took part, with most participants in their first year.

The sessions covered quantum mechanics, superposition, entanglement, quantum algorithms, quantum key distribution, quantum teleportation, quantum optics, post-quantum cryptography and quantum random number generation. The programme combined expert-led sessions with laboratory training, technical demonstrations, interactive discussions and poster presentations.

The QClairvoyance team comprised Afra Navas, Quantum Analyst; Ashish Kumar Patra, Quantum Analyst; and Preet Raj Gupta, Cryptography Analyst. The sessions included practical exercises in quantum gates and circuits using QClairEDU, quantum algorithms, information security and cryptography, along with an introduction to quantum communication and demonstrations of quantum-safe applications. Google Colab was also used during the practical sessions.

The programme was attended by Dr. Ravindra Barlingay, CEO, IITM-CDOT Samgnya Technologies Foundation, through video conference; Dr. Jayaraj U. Kidavu, Executive Director, NIELIT Calicut; Dr. Lakshman Korra, Director In-Charge, NIELIT Hyderabad; Shri C.V. Harish, Deputy Director (Tech), NIELIT Hyderabad; Shri Hemanth Reddy, Technical Officer, NIELIT Hyderabad; and Bharathipudi Srinivas, Vice President, Sales, QClairvoyance Quantum Labs.

Assessment and student feedback:

The workshop concluded on November 13 with a 45-question assessment covering quantum computing, communication, post-quantum cryptography and numerical problem-solving. Of the 109 students who took the test, the average score was 36 out of 45 (80 per cent). As many as 102 scored above 50 per cent, while four students achieved a perfect score.

The final feedback survey, with 73 respondents, recorded an average rating of 4.6 out of 5. More than three-fourths of the respondents said they would recommend the programme to others.

The survey also showed an improvement in students’ understanding of quantum technology. While 15 respondents reported having no prior knowledge before the workshop, none reported the same after its completion. The proportion rating their knowledge as good or very good increased from 42 per cent to 70 per cent. Further, 70 of the 73 respondents said they would or might consider a career in quantum technology or quantum security.

The programme concluded with a valedictory session and distribution of certificates to participants on November 13, giving students an opportunity to take their first steps towards understanding and exploring careers in the growing field of quantum technology.

MENTIONED IN THE ARTICLE

QClairvoyance Quantum Labs specializes in quantum computing applications, focusing on quantum chemistry, drug discovery, and industry-specific quantum software platforms. It develops advanced quantum algorithms and workflows, such as DMET-SQD for molecular simulations, to address challenges in life sciences and other sectors. The company emphasizes practical quantum solutions, collaborating with academic and industry partners to accelerate the adoption of quantum technologies and build a robust quantum ecosystem.
